Hexagonal bins drawn as prisms

Source: R/layers-stats-bins.R
geom_hex_3d.Rd

geom_hex_3d() draws one upright hexagonal prism per row, centred on x and y and extending from the baseline (or zmin) to z. By default it counts observations in hexagonal bins with stat_bin_hex_3d(), the three-dimensional form of ggplot2::geom_hex() and of the extruded hexagon layers of deck.gl. stat_summary_hex_3d() sets each prism's height to a summary of the mapped z values in the hexagon.

Usage

geom_hex_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = StatBinHex3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  width = NULL,
  depth = NULL,
  base = 0,
  cap = "both",
  shade = TRUE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

stat_bin_hex_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomHex3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  bins = 30L,
  binwidth = NULL,
  drop = TRUE,
  base = 0,
  shade = TRUE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

stat_summary_hex_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomHex3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  fun = "mean",
  fun.args = list(),
  bins = 30L,
  binwidth = NULL,
  drop = TRUE,
  base = 0,
  shade = TRUE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

stat

Stat that computes the bins.

width, depth

Hexagon size along x and y; see Details.

base

Baseline of the columns in original z units.

cap

Caps to draw: both, top, bottom or none.

shade

Whether to apply lighting.

geom

Geom used to draw the bins.

bins

Number of bins along x and y.

binwidth

Bin widths along x and y; overrides bins.

drop

For counts, remove empty bins; for summaries, remove bins whose summary is NA.

fun

Summary function, or its name, applied to the z values of each bin; it must return one number.

fun.args

List of further arguments to fun.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

Hexagons have pointed tops. Centres lie binwidth[1] apart along a row and rows lie binwidth[2] * sqrt(3) / 2 apart, every second row shifted by half a hexagon, so the cells are regular when x and y are drawn at the scale of their bin widths; the lattice is anchored at multiples of the bin widths, so groups and panels share it. The default bins = 30 sets the bin widths to a thirtieth of the x and y ranges, as in ggplot2. Each observation goes to the hexagon whose centre is nearest in units of the bin widths.

With stat = "identity", the hexagon size comes from width and depth (columns or arguments): width is the distance between the flat sides, along x, and depth the row spacing divided by sqrt(3) / 2, along y. Without them the size follows from the spacing of the centres.

Computed variables

count

Number of observations in the bin (sum of weights).

density

Count divided by the total count and by the bin area, so the column volumes sum to one.

ncount, ndensity

Count and density divided by their maximum.

width, depth

Bin size along x and y.

value

Summaries only: the result of fun, also used as z.

References

Carr, D. B., Littlefield, R. J., Nicholson, W. L. and Littlefield, J. S. (1987). Scatterplot matrix techniques for large N. Journal of the American Statistical Association 82, 424-436.

See also

stat_bin_2d_3d() for rectangular bins.

Examples

p <- ggplot2::ggplot(faithful, ggplot2::aes(eruptions, waiting))
p + geom_hex_3d(bins = 12) + coord_3d()
p + geom_hex_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = ggplot2::after_stat(count)),
  binwidth = c(0.4, 5), colour = "grey20") + coord_3d()
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(500), y = rnorm(500))
d$z <- d$x^2 + d$y^2
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  stat_summary_hex_3d(bins = 10, fill = "darkorange") + coord_3d()
